note_on_method: Every court count, address, opening time and lighting mark below is quoted from that venue's own entry on the Austin Parks and Recreation Department's pickleball page, and each one is checked against that entry rather than against the page as a whole. The phrase "Lighted during park hours" appears eleven times, so a page-wide check would prove nothing about which park it belongs to. Counties and postcodes come from the Census geocoder. Nobody working on this has played on these courts.

slots.description:
Three dedicated outdoor pickleball courts at the tennis centre attached to Austin High, just west of downtown on Cesar Chavez. What makes this venue different from every other one in Austin is who else has a claim on it: the City states that "the courts at this facility are shared through an agreement between the City of Austin and Austin Independent School District (AISD)", which is why the opening hours follow the school calendar rather than park hours.

Twenty-one of Austin's sixty courts are dedicated pickleball rather than lines on a shared slab, and three of them are here. It is also one of eleven lit venues, and the only one in the whole directory whose opening hours are set by a school district agreement rather than by a parks department. Availability depends on whether Austin schools are in session.
slots.getting_there: 2001 W. Cesar Chavez, Austin, Texas 78703, which the Census geocoder matched to Austin city, Travis County. It is on the river just west of the centre, which makes it one of the most central venues in this directory's Austin set. The City publishes nothing about parking.
slots.what_to_expect: Read the calendar before you go. During the school year the courts open to the public on weekday evenings only, from 5:30 p.m. to 10 p.m. Through the summer months they run seven days a week from 7 a.m. to 10 p.m. During term the school has the daytime. The courts are lit during park hours, so the evening window is real. Nothing is published about nets, surface or cost.

faqs.a: Three, all dedicated pickleball courts rather than lines on a multi-purpose slab. The City's entry reads "3 Dedicated Outdoor Courts".
Monday to Friday from 5:30 p.m. to 10 p.m. during the school year, and seven days a week from 7 a.m. to 10 p.m. during the summer months.
Yes. The City marks this venue "Lighted during park hours". With term-time play starting at 5:30 p.m., the lighting is what makes the venue usable for much of the year.

faqs.q: Do I need to bring a net?
faqs.a: Not stated. Austin states that a net is not provided at three venues and this is not one of them, so the answer here is unknown.

slots.description:
Eight outdoor pickleball courts at Walnut Creek Sports Park in north-east Austin, the largest count in the city by a wide margin, and the only venue in Austin that must be booked. The City marks it "Reservations Required" where every other entry on its pickleball list says Open Play. The courts are lit during park hours, and the facility keeps its own hours rather than the standard park schedule: Monday to Friday 8:30 a.m. to 10:00 p.m., Saturday and Sunday 8:30 a.m. to 9:00 p.m.

Nothing else in the city comes close: Dick Nichols has five and four venues have four. It is the only Austin venue requiring a reservation and, across the ninety-five venues published on this site before Austin, only two others took bookings at all, both of them indoor. This is the closest thing Austin has to a purpose-built pickleball facility.
slots.getting_there: 7800 Johnny Morris Rd., Austin, Texas 78724, matched by the Census geocoder to Austin city, Travis County, in the north-east corner of the city inside Walnut Creek Sports Park. It is the furthest of Austin's venues from the central cluster around Chicon and Rosewood, so this is a drive from most of the city. No parking guidance is published.
slots.what_to_expect: Book first. The City does not publish the booking route or the price on its pickleball page, so call ahead. What you get is the best-equipped pickleball facility in the city: eight courts, floodlit, open until 10 p.m. on weekdays. Surface is not stated, nets are not mentioned either way, and no cost appears anywhere on the page.

faqs.a: Eight outdoor pickleball courts, "8 Outdoor Pickleball Courts" in the City's words. The next largest Austin venue is Dick Nichols District Park with five.

faqs.q: Do I really need a reservation?
faqs.a: The City says so: this is the only entry on its pickleball list marked "Reservations Required" rather than Open Play. Across this whole directory only a handful of other venues take bookings, in other cities.
Monday to Friday, 8:30 a.m. to 10:00 p.m.; Saturday and Sunday, 8:30 a.m. to 9:00 p.m.
Not stated. The City publishes no price on this page.

slots.description:
Four pickleball courts striped onto two multi-purpose outdoor courts at a district park in north-central Austin. The City's entry reads "2 Multi-purpose Outdoor Courts with striping for 4 Pickleball Courts": two physical slabs, four pickleball courts marked on them. The venue is lit during park hours and runs the standard Austin schedule of open play seven days a week, 7 a.m. to 10 p.m. Four courts puts it joint third in the city behind the Austin Tennis and Pickleball Center's eight and Dick Nichols's five.

Four courts on two slabs is the more robust of Austin's two four-court arrangements. At Little Zilker and Mary Moore Searight all four courts sit on a single surface, so one competing use takes the whole venue. Here it would take half.
slots.getting_there: 7000 Ardath St, Austin, TX 78757, matched by the Census geocoder to Austin city, Travis County. It sits in the Allandale and Crestview part of north-central Austin, close to Brentwood Neighborhood Park, the nearest published alternative when four courts are already busy. No parking guidance is published.
slots.what_to_expect: Two slabs shared with whatever else they are marked for, carrying four pickleball courts between them, open 7 a.m. to 10 p.m. every day and lit for the evening half of that. Four courts is enough for a group of eight to rotate without a long wait. Nothing is published about the surface, about nets, or about cost.

faqs.a: Four pickleball courts, striped onto two multi-purpose outdoor courts. Austin gives both numbers and the pickleball figure, four, is the one published here.
Yes, "Lighted during park hours" appears in this venue's entry.

faqs.q: Do I need to bring a net?
faqs.a: Not stated. Austin names three venues where nets are not provided and this is not one of them, so carry one if you have it.

faqs.q: Where else can I play nearby?
faqs.a: Brentwood Neighborhood Park is the closest published venue, with two courts on one slab, also lit. It is one of the three Austin venues that tells you to bring your own portable net.

slots.description:
Two pickleball courts striped onto a single multi-purpose court in the Brentwood neighbourhood of north-central Austin, and one of the few venues anywhere whose operator states that a net is not provided. The City's entry ends "bring your own portable net", a stated negative rather than a silence, which is why this venue's nets field reads No where most venues read "not stated". The courts are lit during park hours and run Austin's standard open-play schedule, seven days a week from 7 a.m. to 10 p.m.

Two courts on one slab is the commonest configuration in Austin, and the lighting mark is what separates this one from most of them. The net statement is what makes it distinctive: three Austin venues say a net is not provided. Most other operators have simply not said, which this site renders as unknown rather than as a promise either way.
slots.getting_there: 6710 Arroyo Seco, Austin, Texas 78757, matched by the Census geocoder to Austin city, Travis County. Arroyo Seco runs through Brentwood in north-central Austin, close to Beverly S. Sheffield Northwest District Park, which has four courts on two slabs and is the obvious alternative if this single slab is taken. No parking information is published.
slots.what_to_expect: Bring a net. The City says it outright. Beyond that: one multi-purpose slab carrying two pickleball courts, shared with whatever else it is striped for, open play seven days a week from 7 a.m. to 10 p.m., lit for the evening half of that. A single group can fill the venue. Surface and cost are not stated.

faqs.q: Do I need to bring a net?
faqs.a: Yes. The City's entry says "bring your own portable net", one of only three Austin venues, and twenty-one venues in this whole directory, where an operator has stated that a net is not provided.

slots.description:
One dedicated pickleball court at a pocket park in north Austin. The City's entry reads "One dedicated pickleball court", the only entry on Austin's list written out in words rather than figures. Dedicated matters: it is a pickleball court rather than lines painted on a slab shared with basketball or tennis, so nobody else has a claim on it.

That makes Delta one of four single-court venues in Austin and one of eight with any dedicated courts at all. The pairing is unusual. Single-court venues are usually striped onto something else, and dedicated courts are usually clustered in larger sets. Here you get a pickleball-only surface at the smallest possible scale.
slots.getting_there: 2325 Donley Dr., Austin, Texas, 78758, matched by the Census geocoder to Austin city, Travis County. Donley Drive is in north Austin near Braker Lane, a short distance from Gustavo "Gus" L. Garcia District Park, which has two striped courts and is the nearest published alternative. No parking guidance is published; on a pocket park, expect the street.
slots.what_to_expect: One court, open play, seven days a week from 7 a.m. to 10 p.m., but no lighting statement, so the late end of those hours is not stated. One dedicated court suits a single game of doubles and nothing larger. Surface, nets and cost are all unstated.

faqs.a: One, dedicated to pickleball. The City writes "One dedicated pickleball court".

slots.description:
Five pickleball courts striped onto two multi-purpose outdoor courts in south-west Austin, the largest open-play count in the city and the largest anywhere in Austin outside the reservation-only Tennis and Pickleball Center. The City states: "2 Multi-purpose Outdoor Courts with striping for 5 Pickleball Courts". It is lit during park hours and runs the standard schedule of open play seven days a week, 7 a.m. to 10 p.m.

Together that makes it, on the published record, the most capable turn-up-and-play venue in Austin. The one thing the record does not tell you is what the courts are made of. Austin states surface nowhere, at any of its twenty-one venues.
slots.getting_there: 8011 Beckett Rd., Austin, Texas 78749, matched by the Census geocoder to Austin city, Travis County. Dick Nichols is a district park in the Oak Hill part of south-west Austin, some way from the central cluster of venues around Chicon and Rosewood. Mary Moore Searight Metro Park, with four courts, is the nearest published alternative to the south-east. No parking information is published.
slots.what_to_expect: The best odds in Austin of getting on a court without booking. Five courts under lights, open until 10 p.m. every day, on two shared slabs, so the courts exist alongside whatever else they are marked for. A busy evening is a real possibility because this is the venue everyone else has also worked out is the good one. Surface is not stated, nets are not mentioned either way, and no price is published.

faqs.a: Five pickleball courts, striped onto two multi-purpose outdoor courts. Only the reservation-only Tennis and Pickleball Center, with eight, is bigger.

slots.description:
Two pickleball courts striped onto one multi-purpose outdoor court in the Enfield area, just west of downtown Austin. The City's entry is brief, "1 Multi-purpose Outdoor with striping for 2 Pickleball Courts", and carries no lighting mark, which places this among the ten Austin venues where the after-dark question is unanswered rather than answered No. The park is named for the Austin-born baseball player Don Baylor.

Two courts on one slab with no lighting statement is the median Austin venue in almost every respect. What lifts it above that median is location. The near-west cluster of Don Baylor, Mary Frances Baylor Clarksville and Austin High Tennis Center puts six courts within a short distance of each other just west of downtown.
slots.getting_there: 2008 Enfield Rd., Austin, Texas 78703, matched by the Census geocoder to Austin city, Travis County. Enfield Road runs west from downtown through Clarksville and Tarrytown. Austin High Tennis Center's three dedicated courts are a short distance south on Cesar Chavez, and Mary Frances Baylor Clarksville's single dedicated court is a few blocks away. Nothing is published about parking.
slots.what_to_expect: One slab, two courts, open play seven days a week from 7 a.m. to 10 p.m., with no lighting statement to support the later end of that. The slab is shared with whatever else it is marked for. Nothing is stated about the surface, about nets, or about cost.

faqs.a: Two pickleball courts, striped onto a single multi-purpose outdoor court.

slots.description:
One dedicated pickleball court at a pocket park on Tannehill Lane in east Austin. The City's entry reads "1 Dedicated Court", and dedicated is the important half: this is a pickleball court rather than lines on a shared slab.

It is also the venue where the City and the Census geocoder disagree about the postcode. The page prints 78702; the geocoder matches the street address and returns 78721. The geocoder's answer is what is published here, as at every venue in this directory, and the disagreement is recorded rather than quietly resolved.
slots.getting_there: 4617 Tannehill Lane, Austin, matched by the Census geocoder to Austin city, Travis County, in the 78721 postcode. The City's own page gives 78702, which covers a different part of east Austin, so if you are searching by postcode rather than street, use the street. Nothing is published about parking; on a pocket park the street is the realistic expectation.

Two pickleball courts striped onto one multi-purpose outdoor court at a district park on East Rundberg Lane in north Austin. The City's entry is the standard form, "1 Multi-purpose Outdoor Court with striping for 2 Pickleball Courts", with no lighting mark, so the after-dark question here is unanswered. The park shares its name and its address with the Gus Garcia Recreation Center, which the City lists separately under indoor pickleball programming; that indoor court is not stated and is not published on this site, so what you see here is the outdoor provision only.

The City runs pickleball at eight recreation centres, indoors, on published schedules. None of it is on record here yet. This venue sits on the seam between the outdoor list and the indoor programme.
slots.getting_there: 1201 E Rundberg Ln., Austin, Texas 78753, matched by the Census geocoder to Austin city, Travis County. This is north Austin between I-35 and Cameron Road. Delta Pocket Park, with a single dedicated court, is the nearest published alternative. No parking guidance appears on the City's page.
slots.what_to_expect: One slab, two pickleball courts, open play seven days a week from 7 a.m. to 10 p.m., with no lighting statement to back the late hours. If the outdoor court is busy, the recreation centre at the same address runs indoor open play on a published schedule, but that programme is not stated, so treat it as a lead rather than a fact. slots.description:
Two pickleball courts striped onto one multi-purpose outdoor court at a recreation centre in central Austin, and the venue with the most restricted schedule in the city, because it follows the centre rather than park hours. During the school year the court is open Monday to Friday from 7 a.m. to 2:30 p.m. and again from 6:30 to 8:30 p.m., with weekends 7 a.m. to 8:30 p.m. On summer and camp days the weekday daytime window disappears and play runs 6:30 to 8:30 p.m. only. No lighting statement is published.

Of Austin's twenty-one venues, twenty are governed by park hours and this one is governed by a building. If you want central Austin with simple hours, Shipe and Patterson are both close by, both lit, and both open 7 a.m. to 10 p.m. every day.
slots.getting_there: 811 E 41st St., Austin, Texas 78751, matched by the Census geocoder to Austin city, Travis County, in Hyde Park north of the university. Patterson Neighborhood Park and Shipe Neighborhood Park, both with two courts and both lit, are the nearest published alternatives. Nothing is published about parking.
slots.what_to_expect: Check the calendar and the clock. This is the only Austin venue whose hours change on both a daily and a seasonal axis, and the gap in the middle of a term-time weekday is four hours long. Two courts on one shared slab, open play rather than booking. Nothing is published about the surface, nets or cost.

slots.description:
Four pickleball courts striped onto a single multi-purpose outdoor court in Zilker, south of the river, the densest striping arrangement in Austin. The City states "1 Multi-purpose Outdoor Courts with striping for 4 Pickleball Courts": four courts marked onto one slab. It is lit during park hours and runs the standard open-play schedule, seven days a week from 7 a.m. to 10 p.m.

Four courts on one slab comes with a specific risk: the whole venue is one asset. At Beverly S. Sheffield or Dick Nichols the courts sit across two slabs, so another use costs you half. Here it costs you everything. Set against that, this is a lit venue with full hours in one of the most desirable parts of the city.
slots.getting_there: 2016 Bluebonnet Ln., Austin, Texas 78704, matched by the Census geocoder to Austin city, Travis County. Bluebonnet Lane is in the Zilker and Barton Hills area just south of Lady Bird Lake. South Austin Neighborhood Park, with two dedicated courts and lights, is the nearest published alternative. No parking guidance is published, and in this neighbourhood that is a real gap.
slots.what_to_expect: Four courts on one slab under lights, open until 10 p.m. daily: a good group venue in a central location. If something else is using the slab, all four courts go at once. Surface, nets and cost are unstated.

One dedicated outdoor pickleball court at a pocket park in Clarksville, the historic freedmen's community just west of downtown Austin. The City's entry reads "1 Dedicated Outdoor Court": a pickleball court rather than lines on a shared slab, which for a single-court venue is the difference between a reliable game and a court that might be in use for something else. There is no lighting statement, so the evening end of the published hours is not stated.

It is part of the near-west cluster with Don Baylor and Austin High Tennis Center. Between them those three venues hold six courts, four of them dedicated. Only Austin High publishes lighting, so for evening play on this side of town Austin High's school-term schedule is the constraint that matters.
slots.getting_there: 1811 W 11th St., Austin, Texas 78703, matched by the Census geocoder to Austin city, Travis County. West 11th Street runs through Clarksville, a short distance from Don Baylor Neighborhood Park's two striped courts on Enfield Road and from Austin High Tennis Center's three dedicated courts on Cesar Chavez. Metro parks are the largest category in the Austin system and this one covers several hundred acres, so the courts are one amenity among many. No lighting statement is published for this venue.

Four courts on one slab, lighting unstated, and no word on where in a very large park they sit: this is the thinnest record of any four-court venue in Austin. It is also the only published pickleball in the far south of the city. Dick Nichols, five courts and lit, is the nearest venue that answers more of the questions, and it is a drive to the west.
slots.getting_there: 907 W Slaughter Ln., Austin, Texas 78748, matched by the Census geocoder to Austin city, Travis County. Slaughter Lane runs across far south Austin. Four courts is enough for a group of eight, provided nothing else is using the slab. Surface, nets and cost are unstated.

This is the largest published venue in north-west Austin, a part of the city where published provision is thin. The only other venues north-west of here are North Lake Creek and Springwoods, both across the county line in Williamson. The city's north-western edge holds six courts across two parks, against twelve courts in the four venues clustered around east Austin's Chicon and Rosewood streets.
slots.getting_there: 8900 Westerkirk Dr., Austin, Texas 78750, matched by the Census geocoder to Austin city, Travis County, in the Anderson Mill and Jollyville part of far north-west Austin. Springwoods Neighborhood Park is the nearest published alternative, a short distance north on Anderson Mill Road, though it has two courts rather than four and requires you to bring a net. As the largest published venue in north-west Austin it is the default for that part of the city, and worth arriving at early on a pleasant evening for the same reason. The City's entry reads "1 Multi-purpose Outdoor Court with striping for 1 Pickleball Court", the smallest configuration on Austin's list: one slab, one court. No lighting statement is published.

It earns its place on this site for two reasons beyond the court itself: it is one of two Austin venues the Census places in Williamson County rather than Travis, and it is one of two where the City's postcode and the geocoder's disagree. The page prints 78753; the geocoder returns 78717. Both are ordinary facts about a large city that spills across boundaries, and both are recorded rather than smoothed over.
slots.getting_there: 9201 North Lake Creek, Austin, matched by the Census geocoder to Austin city, Williamson County, in the 78717 postcode, not the 78753 the City's page prints. This is the far north of the city near the Round Rock and Cedar Park edge. No parking guidance is published.

slots.description:
Four courts on Chicon Street in east Austin: three dedicated outdoor pickleball courts plus one multi-purpose court striped for a fourth, lit during park hours, and carrying the most complicated schedule in the city. The City states it outright: "Courts unavailable on Tuesday and Thursday from 7 to 10 p.m. and Saturday and Sunday from 9 a.m. to 12 p.m. for roller derby practice." That is a genuinely useful sentence, and one no other operator in this directory has published: a named competing use, with exact times, on specific days.

Four courts, three of them dedicated, lit, and closer to downtown than any comparable venue: on paper this is one of the two best sites in Austin. The roller derby schedule is what complicates it, and it is also what makes this entry unusually valuable: no other operator in this directory has published a named competing use with exact days and times. Austin tells you in advance when the courts are taken.
slots.getting_there: 307 Chicon St., Austin, Texas 78702, matched by the Census geocoder to Austin city, Travis County, in east Austin close to the centre and part of the densest cluster of published venues in the city alongside Rosewood, Patterson and Eastside Pocket Park. No parking guidance is published for the park.
slots.what_to_expect: Check the day before you go. The City publishes hours of Monday, Wednesday and Friday 7 a.m. to 10 p.m.; Tuesday and Thursday 7 a.m. to 7 p.m.; Saturday and Sunday 7 a.m. to 9 a.m. So weekend play is a two-hour morning window. Within those hours you get four courts, three of them dedicated, under lights. Surface, nets and cost are not stated.

faqs.a: Four: three dedicated outdoor courts plus one multi-purpose court striped for one more.

faqs.q: When can I play at the weekend?
faqs.a: Between 7 a.m. and 9 a.m. on Saturday and Sunday, according to the City's published hours. After 9 a.m. the courts go to roller derby until noon.
